summary:
ARES-4: NO RELIEF is a browser game where kids ages 7–12 lead a 150-person Mars colony whose supply ship never arrived. Each Martian week, a colonist, specialist or Mission Control presents a problem, and the player swipes left or right. Every choice changes four meters: oxygen, food, energy and morale. No choice is free: running the generators can drain the air, and pushing the crew can break morale. If any meter hits 0 or 100, the colony fails, so the goal is balance. Survive 100 weeks until the next launch window to win.

The game turns real deep-space constraints into play: solar storms and radiation, dust storms that starve solar panels, toxic soil, oxygen made from CO₂ like NASA’s MOXIE experiment, and 26-month transfer windows. Short science facts follow decisions and appear on the end screen in plain language. Shuffled cards, rising difficulty, rare Mission Control events and 9 collectible endings make failure a reason to replay. It needs no download or account.
details:
What it does and how it works
ARES-4: NO RELIEF is a swipe-card strategy game for kids ages 7–12. The player is the new Captain of a 150-person Mars colony whose supply ship never arrived. Each card is one Martian week: a colonist, a specialist or Mission Control presents a problem with two choices. Every choice changes four meters: oxygen (life support), food, energy (power) and morale. While dragging a card, the game only highlights which meters will change, not by how much, so players must reason about the trade-off. If any meter hits 0 or 100, the colony fails, with 9 different endings. Surviving 100 weeks until the next transfer window wins the game, and players can keep going afterwards.

Benefits and intended impact
No choice is free: saving power can cost air, and pushing the crew can cost morale. Kids learn that deep-space survival is about balance, not a single right answer. Short plain-language science facts follow decisions and appear on the end screen. Failure is part of the fun, because 9 collectible endings, a best-score record, rising difficulty and shuffled cards encourage replay and new strategies. It runs in any browser with no download or account, so it works in classrooms and on phones.

Science content and honesty about data
Scenarios are based on real Mars facts: the 24 h 39 min sol, radio delays up to 22 minutes, toxic perchlorates in the soil, oxygen from CO₂ like NASA’s MOXIE experiment, dust storms, radiation and 26-month launch windows. These facts are curated by hand from public NASA information, not pulled live from an API. Connecting archived NASA DONKI space-weather events is our planned next step.

Tools
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks, libraries or build step. Music and sound effects are generated in code with the Web Audio API, progress is saved with localStorage, and the game is hosted on GitHub Pages. [Describe any AI tools used, for example for code assistance or artwork.]

Creativity and design factors
We combined the Reigns-style swipe format with a Mars survival story and a mystery about the vanished previous Captain, revealed through rare golden Mission Control cards. Four teammates worked in parallel by agreeing on a fixed card and engine contract. We kept the interface simple for young players, with keyboard and touch support, adjustable sound, a first-run hint and reduced-motion support.
